licence_research.summary: Commercial use of the Tripo outputs depends on the account being a paid account, which could not be confirmed. Treat every Tripo-sourced mesh as NOT cleared for commercial release until the account owner confirms the tier (paid subscription, or API credits bought rather than granted).

findings: s3.2: Outputs may be used 'for lawful commercial or non-commercial purposes', but not to build models or services that directly compete with Holymolly (Tripo's operator); no guarantee of exclusivity.
s5.2.1 Free users: 'Tripo retains all rights, including without limitation the rights to use, copy, reproduce, modify' the Inputs and Outputs.

s5.2.2 Paid users: 'generally have all rights' over Inputs and Outputs, subject to a royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to the company; the company will not train on them.
s6.4: API Credits are 'intended primarily for business and professional use' and are 'prepaid and non-refundable once purchased'.
No attribution requirement is stated for Outputs.
Pay-as-you-go API credits, 1 credit = 0.01 USD; text-to-3D 10 credits untextured, 20 with standard texture (H-series figures; P-series tasks here were charged 40 credits each).
Says nothing about licensing or commercial use.

sources.fetched: not fetched: the site answered HTTP 403 to automated requests
findings: A search-engine summary of this official help page says commercial use requires a paid plan and that free users' outputs belong to Tripo (terms s5.2.1). Not read directly; listed so it can be checked by hand.

account.tier: unverified: the API exposes a credit balance only, not the plan. A prepaid API credit balance suggests purchased credits (s6.4), but granted or trial credits cannot be ruled out.
